vulnerability.title: Netty Bzip2Decoder accumulates all decompressed blocks of one input buffer instead of streaming them, allowing memory-exhaustion denial of service

fixed_releases.verified_content: At the 4.1.68 release commit (7d34282f) Bzip2Decoder returns after each block and Bzip2BlockDecompressor rejects bwtBlockLength above MAX_BLOCK_LENGTH

severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD Primary CVSS 3.1 is 7.5 High and the GHSA/OSV label is HIGH with the same vector; the CNA publishes no numeric score. The legacy NVD CVSS v2 score is 5.0 Medium.
severity.ghsa_label_note: GHSA/OSV labels the issue HIGH and publishes the same CVSS 3.1 vector; it carries no separate numeric base score.

vulnerability.category_l2: Decompression: decode() retains every block output in the out list until the input buffer is exhausted, so heap use scales with total decompressed size rather than one block

critical_operation.description: Bzip2Decoder.decode() handles a whole input buffer in one loop. For each compressed block it allocates an output buffer, inflates the block into it, adds it to the out list and then breaks back into the loop rather than returning. ByteToMessageDecoder.callDecode() flushes out only after decode() returns, so every block decompressed from one input buffer stays resident at the same time. Heap use therefore scales with the total decompressed size of the input buffer rather than with one block, and a small crafted bzip2 stream that decompresses to a very large output can exhaust the heap (CWE-400). The 4.1.68 fix returns after each block so buffers are propagated and released incrementally; its added MAX_BLOCK_LENGTH check is defense-in-depth on top of the existing streamBlockSize bounds, not the reachable defect.

entry_point.description: An attacker-controlled peer sends a bzip2-compressed byte stream to a channel pipeline that includes Bzip2Decoder; the stream decompresses to far more data than the peer sends.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No bzip2 stream was crafted and no JVM heap exhaustion was attempted; impact is established statically from the buffering and allocation path.
Only the 4.1 branch was inspected; other codec modules and native transports were not audited.
The practical memory ceiling depends on the application pipeline, heap size and how quickly downstream handlers release buffers.

The missing MAX_BLOCK_LENGTH check in 4.1.59 is not a reachable oversized-block path because the existing streamBlockSize checks already bound bwtBlockLength; only the non-streaming accumulation is treated as the root cause.
open_questions: The exact compression ratio needed to exhaust a given heap was not measured.
Whether a caller that drains out per block can fully avoid the accumulation for a single oversized input buffer was not tested.
